utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness 269, I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony yesterday and Ms. Hochhauser you may proceed with your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and good morning. Could I ask that we return to private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can we please have Exhibit P1132 on the monitor at page 131?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If by the way the Chamber was overcautious in admitting it under seal, could you please consider to what extent it's really needed so that if it can be made public that we change that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye and I were having that conversation by eye, so I'll get back to you after the break about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise what's on the screen in front of us now?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's the physical education gymnasium at the Orahovac primary cool.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the location that you discuss in your prior testimony?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us the -- where it's marked entrance and exit on this photograph, did -- is that accurate, to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can we turn, please, to page 130, the page before, on the monitor? And if we could zoom in so that only the picture on the left that's marked "gym" is on the screen, and if I could actually ask again for the assistance of the usher so that the witness can mark on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to ask you if we are now looking at the outside of the same building, of the gymnasium?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark for us, please, with an E from the outside the corresponding -- the entrance. So what we saw on the inside marked as entrance, can you mark where it is on the outside of the building with an E and then the same with an X for the exit?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us what you observed Nada Stojanovic doing at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we all had pretty much the same role, and that was to secure the building and the individuals inside it. I was in a group of several people at the entrance, whereas Nada would occasionally come to us, she would walk around the school, she would go to the road. Specifically her duty, or at least that's what I saw her doing, was when prisoners were being taken out and loaded on to trucks, I saw her and another policeman, two or three individuals, soldiers, at the exit. The driver of that little truck may have been with them. And I saw them moving tied up individuals on to trucks. As this was going on, people inside were complaining they didn't know what it meant, where they were being taken in such rather small groups. So I was at the entranceway, and focused on pacifying the mass of people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "moving tied up individuals on to trucks," can you tell us whether you actually saw the people being bound, and in what -- in what way were they bound?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't be precise enough to tell you what they were bound with. Was it wire? I can't be sure. At any rate, I am definitely certain that they were bound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see any of the prisoners there blindfolded?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know with what degree of certainty I can state this but I do believe that I saw Nada putting blindfolds on. Now, was this something that Nada was supposed to do in respect of every individual, well, I didn't really pay that much attention to that, as I did to the entrance where the mass of people was, by that time, greatly upset.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the past several responses, you have referred to people by the entrance, people by the exit. What we have marked on the screen now where you've marked the entrance and the exit from the outside of the building, is -- does that reflect where you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to tender the marked exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document as marked by the witness receives number P1566, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could turn for a moment, please in this same -- same -- the same item of evidence, the photo book, P1132, to page 164? I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I have the wrong -- I have the wrong number -- page. I apologise. I believe it's page 186.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, if you could take a look at this page, 186, that's on the monitor now and then if we could also flip to page 187, the next page, and can you just identify for us whether this reflects one of the locations that you discuss in your testimony -- in your previous testimony? And what is that location?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's the primary school at Rocevici.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, that concludes my examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hochhauser. You've shown the witness two pictures. My recollection doesn't serve me. 186 and 187 is the same building from different sides? Is that --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Well, I can leave that to the witness rather than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Of course, we have testimony about what it depicts but the two pictures shown to you, I think -- yes. There is one on the screen. Both the pictures, the one seems to be a bit of a darker building, the other one seems to be a more white building, is that the same building from different sides?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good morning.

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. You'll find him to your left. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell the Chamber what time of day it was that you received an order from your company commander to set off in the direction of Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I start by saying, without taking up too much of your time, that time didn't play much of a role to me. My time was disposed of by others and I did not really pay attention to what day it was or what time of day, though I can tell you that I believe it was after breakfast.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber how much time it took you to reach the school at Orahovac from the Zvornik Brigade HQ?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not more than 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you got there, prisoners had not arrived yet; right?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How much time passed after you arrived there and after the preparations you referred to, that buses started finally arriving?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite soon, an hour, half an hour, or perhaps a bit more than an hour later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your best estimate, a dozen buses arrived; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were they civilian buses?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber who secured the buses and who escorted them?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the civilian police did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were all prisoners from these buses put up in the gymnasium that you were looking at a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: There were no prisoners in the classrooms of the school?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At one point, the inhabitants of these villages started assembling?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain or describe the situation, what it was like? Was there a risk of an incident happening?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. There was confusion and commotion, as the buses started arriving, people grew ever more curious. The school is located centrally in the village. People started gathering spontaneously. Am I speaking slowly enough for the sake of interpretation? They started gathering. Frankly, they did not take trouble to conceal at all their anger and hatred, which were quite understandable up to a point because there was nobody in that crowd of people who didn't lose someone among their nearest and dearest.

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) There was a large group of Muslims breaking heir way through that area in the direction of Tuzla, so there was fighting going on there. We were in such a position that we didn't know where to look first or where to turn first. We turned toward the prisoners in the school because they could hear a lot of noise and shouting, an odd bullet being fired outside. People were frustrated. Some of the people outside were visibly intoxicated, brandishing weapons. You had to be cautious in approaching these people and dealing with them. It was very dangerous. So we had ever more problems with the group as it grew in numbers eventually.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if that unhappy crowd of people, disgruntled crowd of people, did they ask for the people inside to be liquidated, to be killed, that revenge be taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted) He asked me what I was doing there so I explained to him that I had been wounded so I was assigned here to take some rest. He asked me then, Well, what are you waiting for? We should kill them all. And then I said, Well, take it slowly. This isn't the manner in which this should be approached. But you could already tell by looking at these people that they were passed the stage of being spoken to or reasoned with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic -- or Ms. Hochhauser?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I was going to ask that we go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we may do that. Before we do so, Mr. Stojanovic, approximately 95 per cent of the evidence that you are eliciting from this witness at this moment is found in his statement and I have not heard one question which seems to challenge or to dispute anything which is found in his statement. So therefore I'm wondering what we are -- what we are doing. The only thing is you add a few details to what is presented as evidence by the Prosecution. Could you please focus on what is in dispute and could you please not repeat the evidence just to say, for example, killing? Comments along the lines, all of them ought to be killed, that's what the witness said already. We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in your best estimation, how many prisoners were brought there on these ten-odd buses?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I'm in a position to say. The buses were quite full. There were some people standing, and if you consider that some 50 to 60 individuals can stand and there may have been more than ten buses, I even expressed a reservation in one of the statements that there may have been as many as 15 buses but not more, so I would guess between 700 and 800 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall if some other units passed by Orahovac in the direction of Baljkovica at the time that you were in front of the school?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The road was otherwise used for those who went to man the lines at Baljkovica, Kitovnica. I think it was under the 6th Battalion but I'm not sure. Many of them would linger as they passed by, slow down, because they were trying to see what was going on. Some of them stopped and stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You, yourself, never went to the place where executions were carried out?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You personally don't know who participated in these executions, do you?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, when was the last group of prisoners taken out of the gymnasium?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At dusk, just before it became dark. At that time it was already over.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the order that you received from your company commander to provide security to the school building and to prevent any possible acts of revenge, did you at any point receive a different or a new order?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you this - we are in public session - can you tell us if, as you were performing your tasks, more military policemen from the Zvornik Brigade came there at some point?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not policemen, no, but some members of the Zvornik Brigade came along with us who happened to be down there. As I said, the majority of personnel were at Baljkovica because that was where the much-talked-about breakthrough was ongoing and where there was fighting going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know an individual by the Gojko Simic?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name is familiar, but I cannot remember him now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps this is a good time for the break because I'm going to be using another document. So perhaps we can do that after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is, Mr. Stojanovic. For the witness to leave the courtroom, we briefly turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Stojanovic, once you're ready and once the curtains are up, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at P1565 in e-court, and this is a document under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And while we are waiting for the document to be shown, Witness, let's just go back to the document that you were able to see a little bit earlier. Do you know who maintained this record of attendance of members of your unit? Don't mention your unit, please.

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I name the person?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps then it would be better to move into private session for this particular topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, at one point the following day, you received an order to go to the Rocevic school; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you go with to the school in Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Jasikovac and with a military policeman by the name of Cane -- nicknamed Cane.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell me specifically what your order said for that day?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same as for the previous day in Orahovac, to secure the place, not allow civilians in, because the school is also in the centre of the village, so we were to prevent the villagers from approaching or coming close to the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was the atmosphere among the inhabitants of that village different than the one you described in front of the school in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it was slightly less intense, because judging by the way these people looked and by their conduct, we assumed that these were villagers, they were armed, some were visibly drunk. That was when I noticed five or six dead bodies around the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One question to clarify. When asked about what you were ordered to do, you said more or less that you should protect the prisoners against the villagers. May I take it that it was also part of your task to take care that the prisoners would stay where they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the prisoners to stay where they were and for us to secure the facility, to secure or guard the facility where they were located, and to try and prevent others from getting to them. Meaning the local population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The prisoners shouldn't go out and the villagers should not go in, is that what your task was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find at any point in time how those five or six bodies came to be there, how were those people killed?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the time we arrived, they had already been put up in the gymnasium; in other words, it wasn't the same as it had been in Orahovac where we were waiting for them and received them. When we got there, they were already in the gym. We heard off the record that it was one of the local men there who had lost a member of their family, apparently a man who had lost his son and then took out a couple of these individuals from the gym and killed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to recognise any of the individuals who were there before you, as security for the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really. I only saw - and this is my opinion - that they recognised each other, that they recognised the villagers as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the two of you and your company commander, were there any other members of your unit there on that day that you observed?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can say that there were many soldiers there. Now, did I recognise any of them? No. I can't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't see anyone either from the MP company of the Zvornik Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When did the boarding and transportation of these individuals start?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the time we got there, it was already underway. They were already dealing with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who boarded and transported prisoners?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: People in uniform. They wore uniforms of the VRS. I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't go to the site where these people were being transported and executed?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know who did it specifically, do you?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As you were outside the school in Orahovac on the first day, did you see General Mladic at any point?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did there come a time that you left the unit you were a part of in the Zvornik Brigade, a couple of days later?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, we move briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me finish with one more question. After this assignment outside the school in Rocevic, did you have any other duties concerning prisoners?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, thank you. The Defence has no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Ms. Hochhauser, has the cross-examination triggered any need for further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Your Honour, perhaps three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Witness, are you aware that there were military police officers that went to Orahovac to guard prisoners the night before you went so that it would be the evening of the 13th? Do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no personal knowledge of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: On today's temporary transcript at page 19, line 15 through 17, you were asked the question: "You personally don't know who participated in these executions, do you?" And you answered: "No." And that was in regard to the executions of the prisoners taken out of the Orahovac school. Now, in Exhibit P1561, at e-court pages 21 through 23, you described the fact that soldiers from the Zvornik Brigade - and on at least one occasion accompanied also by Zvornik Brigade MPs - came back with the empty buses talking about the fact that prisoners had been killed; is that right? You heard these soldiers talking about the fact that prisoners were being killed when they arrived back from the site?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And did you see -- well, just to be clear, those -- those men who were talking or soldiers who were talking about prisoners being killed, were the same men that had accompanied the buses full of soldiers, full of prisoners and then come back to the school with empty buses shortly thereafter; correct?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two policemen were also charged with being escorts of these buses. However, when the vehicle left the compound and went down the road to the execution site, many others joined. Now, was it to make an impression on those who were by the road side and looking on? Some were boasting, firing the ammunition that they had in their barrels. I only saw once that military policemen were with the truck as it was driving down the road. I don't know if it was their duty to be escorting every single vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: When you say others joined and were firing the ammunition they had in their barrels, we are talking about soldiers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And those were soldiers that you recognised as of the Zvornik -- recognised - I don't mean personally but by uniform - as being -- by uniform. And from their interaction with the crowd, I believe you say in the statement, as being from the Zvornik Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Did you also see them at any point when they returned cleaning their guns?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would recharge their ammunition clips, et cetera. But, again, I repeat, I was focused on that other crowd. I would just cast glances at them. I was still focused on the entrance. There were people who were very much agitated by that point. They had heard gun shots and knew that something was amiss.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And when you say that there were people there who were hearing gun shots and knew that something was amiss, you've also described that there were local people around the area at -- at around the school at Orahovac. Was it -- was it clear from your observations of everybody that was there that -- that they could hear the gunshots and were aware that something was going on?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they could and they could have supposed it. The small truck would take a smallish group of people, I don't know how many could fit, and very soon it would come back and the trip would be repeated again. I think that they were aware that this was about an execution.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: So just to be clear, it was -- it was obvious to you at the time that these people were being executed, and was it your impression that it was obvious to the -- tot he others that were gathered there?

utterances.speaker: RM269 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: That concludes my redirect examination, Your Honours. Thank you for the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hochhauser. No further questions. Then, Witness, I'd like to thank you very much because this concludes your examination in this Court.
